gloss: open; loose, set free; engrave; opening, entrance
summary: פָּתַח is to open what was shut: a door, gate or window, a sack or skin, a cave, a grave, the womb, the hand to give and the mouth to speak; Yahweh opens the windows of the heavens and his storehouse, and he opens graves to bring his people up (Ezk 37:12). Its piel is to loose what binds, a girdle, a load, a prisoner’s bonds (Psa 116:16), and also to engrave stone and metal, as the names of Israel’s sons on the high priest’s onyx stones (Exo 28:9–11). פֶּתַח is the opening itself, the doorway of a house, tent or city, and above all “the entrance of the tent of meeting”, where Israel brought its offerings and assembled at the trumpets (Num 10:3); מַפְתֵּחַ is the key that opens. The verb, the noun “doorway” and the noun “key” are the same root in Arabic, Akkadian, Ugaritic, Phoenician, Aramaic and Ge’ez, and Phoenician also has the noun “engraving”.

senses.definition: To open what closes a way in or out, a door, gate or window, so that someone may pass or something be let through; its opposite is to shut (סָגַר).

evidence.note: Noah opened the window of the ark.
“He will open and none will shut, and he will shut and none will open”: פָּתַח set against סָגַר.
Eglon was not opening the doors, so his servants took the key (מַפְתֵּחַ) and opened them.
The beloved knocks: “Open to me, my sister.”
“Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter them.”
“Open the gates, that the righteous nation may enter.”
Samuel opened the doors of the house of Yahweh in the morning.
Hezekiah opened the doors of the house of Yahweh in the first month of his reign.
“Open the window eastward”, before the arrow of victory.
“I opened my doors to the traveller.”
The east gate is opened for the prince’s freewill offering.
The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until after the sabbath.
“Open the mouth of the cave.”
“Open your doors, Lebanon, that fire may devour your cedars.”

senses.gloss: open a city, land; lay open
senses.definition: Of a city, to open its gates to an enemy, to surrender; of a land or its flank, to be laid open to invasion; a city left “open” has no one guarding it.

evidence.note: If a city answers peace “and opens to you”, its people become forced labour.
Menahem struck Tiphsah “because it did not open”.
They left Ai open and pursued Israel.
The cities of the Negev are shut up, “and there is none to open”.
“I am opening the flank of Moab” to the men of the east.
The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies.

senses.gloss: open a container, a store; sell grain
senses.definition: To open a sack, skin, basket, pit or storehouse, so as to take out what is inside; Joseph opened the granaries to sell grain, and the merchants of Amos’s day wait for the sabbath to pass to “open” wheat, to sell it. Yahweh opens his treasure, the heavens, to give rain, and his armoury to bring out his weapons.

evidence.note: One of the brothers opened his sack and saw his silver.
Jael opened a skin of milk and gave Sisera drink.
Pharaoh’s daughter opened the basket and saw the child.
A man who opens a pit and does not cover it.
Joseph opened all that was in them and sold grain to Egypt.
“When will the sabbath be past, that we may open wheat?”, set beside selling grain.
“Yahweh will open to you his good treasure, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its season.”
“If I will not open for you the windows of the heavens and pour out a blessing.”
He commanded the clouds and opened the doors of the heavens, and rained manna.
Yahweh has opened his armoury and brought out the weapons of his indignation.
“Open her granaries.”
Ezra opened the book before all the people, and as he opened it they stood.
Sanballat’s open letter, unsealed for all to read.
Every open vessel with no covering bound on it is unclean.

senses.definition: With “mouth” or “lips”, to begin to speak, or to be given speech; not to open the mouth is silence, the dumb man’s and the servant’s who bore affliction without a word.

evidence.note: “Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.”
“I was mute; I did not open my mouth.”
“Like a mute man who does not open his mouth.”
The servant “did not open his mouth”; like a lamb led to slaughter and a ewe dumb before her shearers. Quoted Act 8:32.
“I will open my mouth in a parable.” Quoted Mat 13:35.
“Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.”
Yahweh opened the mouth of the donkey, and she spoke.
“When I speak with you I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them.”
He opened my mouth, and I was no longer mute.
“I opened my mouth, and he made me eat the scroll.”
“Open your mouth for the mute.”
“She opens her mouth with wisdom.”
In the gate the fool does not open his mouth.
A wicked and deceitful mouth have they opened against me.
“To open the mouth with slaughter”, to raise the war cry.

senses.definition: To open a dark saying, to set it out and make it plain.

evidence.note: “I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will open my riddle on the harp.”
Opening the mouth in a parable, pouring out riddles from of old.

senses.gloss: open the earth’s mouth; open springs
senses.definition: Of the earth, to open its mouth and swallow; of Yahweh, to open springs and rivers from rock and bare heights; of the earth in Isaiah, to open and bring forth salvation.

evidence.note: “The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them”, Korah’s company.
“The earth opened and swallowed Dathan.”
He opened the rock and waters gushed out.
“I will open rivers on the bare heights.”
“Let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation.”

senses.definition: Of God, to give a barren woman children.

evidence.note: Yahweh saw that Leah was hated, and opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
God remembered Rachel and opened her womb.

senses.definition: To open the hand is to give, to the poor brother, or of Yahweh to every living thing.

evidence.note: “You shall surely open your hand to him and lend him enough for his need”, against shutting the hand (v. 7).
“You open your hand; they are satisfied with good.”
“You open your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing.”

senses.gloss: open the ear; eyes open (to hear prayer)
senses.definition: Yahweh opens the servant’s ear to hear and obey; in prayer, Yahweh’s eyes are asked to be “open” toward the house and the one who prays, attentive to hear.

evidence.note: “The Lord Yahweh has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious.”
“That your eyes may be open toward this house night and day, to hear the prayer.”
Open eyes and attentive ears, in parallel.

senses.definition: Yahweh opens his people’s graves to bring them up alive; an “open grave” is a picture of a throat that devours, and of a quiver that brings death.

evidence.note: “Behold, I am opening your graves, and I will bring you up from your graves, my people.”
“Their throat is an open grave.” Quoted Rom 3:13.
Their quiver is an open grave.

senses.definition: To open a sword is to draw it from its sheath, ready to kill.

evidence.note: “The wicked have drawn the sword and bent their bow, to cast down the poor.”
“A sword, a sword drawn for the slaughter.”

senses.definition: To open the way home for prisoners, to let them go.

evidence.note: The king of Babylon “did not open the house to his prisoners”, did not let them go home.

senses.definition: Of a root, to lie open to the water.

evidence.note: “My root is open to the waters, and the dew lodges on my branch.”

stems.gloss: be opened; be loosed, let loose

senses.definition: Of the windows and doors of the heavens, gates, a fountain, the mouth and ears: to be opened, often by Yahweh.

evidence.note: All the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the heavens were opened.
“The windows from on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth shake.”
“The heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.”
“This gate shall be shut; it shall not be opened”, because Yahweh entered by it.
The inner east gate shut on the six working days, opened on the sabbath and the new moon.
The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace melts.
“A fountain opened for the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.”
“The ears of the deaf shall be opened”, beside the opened eyes of the blind (פָּקַח).
“On that day your mouth will be opened and you will speak, and be mute no more.”
“He shuts a man up, and there is no opening”, set against סָגַר.
Elihu’s belly is like wine that has no vent, about to burst.

senses.definition: Of a girdle, to come undone; of a captive, to be set free; of disaster, to be let loose.

evidence.note: The invader’s girdle is not loosed, his sandal strap not broken.
The one bowed down in fetters will soon be set free, and will not die in the pit.
“Out of the north disaster will be let loose on all the inhabitants of the land.”

stems.gloss: loose, ungird, set free; open; engrave

senses.definition: To undo what binds: a load from camels, a girdle or sackcloth from the loins, cords and bonds, and so to set a prisoner free.

evidence.note: “I am your servant… you have loosed my bonds.”
The king sent and released Joseph; the ruler of peoples set him free (פִּתַּח), in parallel with הִתִּיר.
The fast Yahweh chooses: “to loose the bonds of wickedness, to undo the bands of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free.”
“I loose you today from the chains on your hands.”
To hear the groaning of the prisoner, to set free those appointed to death.
Who has loosed the bonds of the wild donkey?
“Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades, or loose the cords of Orion?”: loosing set against binding.
He looses the bond of kings.
Abraham’s servant came in and he ungirded (unloaded) the camels.
“Let not him who girds on boast as one who takes off (his armour).”
“Loose the sackcloth from your loins.”
“You have loosed my sackcloth and girded me with gladness.”
“I will loose the loins of kings”, ungird them, to open doors before Cyrus.

senses.definition: To open, as the qal: gates standing open, an ear open to hear, the doors of the crocodile’s face, blossoms opening, and ground broken open by the plough.

evidence.note: “Your gates shall be open continually; day and night they shall not be shut.”
“From of old your ear was not opened”; Israel did not hear.
“Who can open the doors of his face?”
To see whether the blossom has opened.
Does the ploughman keep opening and harrowing his ground?

senses.definition: To cut letters or figures into stone, gold or wood: the names of Israel’s sons on the onyx stones, “Holy to Yahweh” on the gold plate, cherubim on the temple’s walls and stands; and Yahweh’s own engraving on the stone set before Joshua.

evidence.note: “Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel.”
The work of an engraver in stone, “the engravings of a signet”.
On the plate of pure gold, engraved like a signet: “Holy to Yahweh.”
He engraved cherubim, lions and palm trees on the stands.
He engraved cherubim on the walls of the house.
A man skilled “to engrave engravings”.
On the one stone with seven eyes: “Behold, I will engrave its engraving… and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.”

senses.definition: Of the onyx stones, to have the names of the tribes cut into them.

evidence.note: The onyx stones, “engraved with the engravings of a signet, with the names of the sons of Israel”.

senses.definition: To free oneself of what binds; Zion is called to shake off her captivity.

evidence.note: “Shake yourself from the dust; arise… loose yourself from the bonds of your neck, captive daughter of Zion.”

evidence.locator: Psa.78.2, פָּתַח → ἀνοίγω; Isa.53.7, Num.16.32, Ezk.37.12, Gen.7.11 the same; ἀνοίγω renders פָּתַח ×73

evidence.note: “I will open my mouth in parables”, quoting Psa 78:2 of Jesus’ teaching.
Isa 53:7, “so he opened not his mouth”, read by the eunuch; Philip preached Jesus from it (v. 35).
“He who has the key of David, who opens and no one shuts”, Isa 22:22.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river, in the words of Num 16:32.
“Their throat is an open grave”, Psa 5:10.
The graves were opened, and many bodies of the saints arose.

evidence.locator: Psa.102.21, פָּתַח → λῦσαι; Job.39.5 → ἔλυσεν; Isa.58.6 → λῦε; Jer.40.4 → ἔλυσα

evidence.note: The daughter of Abraham bound eighteen years, loosed from this bond on the sabbath.
The bond of the deaf man’s tongue was loosed.

parallels.note: The king “released” Joseph; the ruler “set him free”.
Loosing the bonds of wickedness beside letting the oppressed go free.

opposites.note: Shut: he opens and none shuts, he shuts and none opens; gates open day and night, never shut.
Shutting the hand against the poor brother, against opening it.
Binding the Pleiades against loosing Orion’s cords.

phrases.gloss: the windows of the heavens were opened

senses.gloss: entrance of the tent of meeting
senses.definition: The doorway of the tabernacle, where the altar of burnt offering stood, where every offering was brought and slain, where the priests were washed and ordained, and where the congregation gathered to Yahweh and he met them.

evidence.note: “When they blow both trumpets, all the congregation shall gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.”
A continual burnt offering “at the entrance of the tent of meeting before Yahweh, where I will meet with you, to speak to you there”.
The burnt offering brought “to the entrance of the tent of meeting, that he may be accepted before Yahweh”.
An ox not brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting is blood guilt to the man who slew it.
Aaron and his sons brought to the entrance and washed.
The priests not to go out from the entrance for the seven days of ordination.
The two goats set before Yahweh at the entrance on the day of coverings.
The Nazirite brought to the entrance at the end of his days.
Korah gathers the congregation to the entrance, and the glory of Yahweh appears.
Zelophehad’s daughters stand before Moses and the congregation at the entrance.
The pillar of cloud stood at the entrance of the tent and spoke with Moses.
The land divided by lot before Yahweh at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The screen for the entrance of the tent.
The altar of burnt offering set before the entrance.

senses.gloss: door of a house, tent, ark, cave
senses.definition: The opening by which one goes in and out of a dwelling: the door of the ark, of Abraham’s tent, of Lot’s and the Levite’s houses, of Elijah’s cave; with דֶּלֶת, the door that closes it.

evidence.note: “The door of the ark you shall set in its side.”
Abraham sat at the door of the tent in the heat of the day.
Lot went out to them at the doorway and shut the door (דֶּלֶת) behind him: the opening and its door told apart.
The woman fell at the door of the man’s house.
Brought out to the door of her father’s house.
At the Passover none shall go out of the door of his house until morning.
Yahweh will pass over the door and not let the destroyer come in.
The people weeping, each at the door of his tent.
Elijah stood at the entrance of the cave.
The foolish woman sits at the door of her house.
“Do not go near the door of her house.”
“Watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.”

senses.gloss: gate, entrance of a city or temple
senses.definition: The opening of a city’s gate, where elders sat and kings held court, and the doorways and entrances of the temple and its chambers.

evidence.note: The manslayer stands at the entrance of the gate of the city and speaks his case to the elders.
The kings sat at the entrance of the gate of Samaria.
Tamar sat at the entrance of Enaim.
Wisdom cries at the openings of the gates.
The kings of the north set their thrones at the entrance of Jerusalem’s gates.
Her gates lament and mourn.
The land of Nimrod at its entrances.
The entrance of the inner sanctuary, with doors of olive wood.
At the entrance of the temple, between the porch and the altar, men bowing to the sun.
The people bow at the entrance of the gate on sabbaths and new moons.
Waters coming out from under the threshold at the entrance of the house.
“Lift up your heads, O gates, and be lifted up, everlasting doors (פִּתְחֵי עוֹלָם), that the King of glory may come in”: פֶּתַח parallel to שַׁעַר.

senses.definition: A way in for sin, for hope, or for words: sin crouching at Cain’s door; the valley of Achor made a door of hope; the doors of the mouth kept shut from a companion.

evidence.note: “If you do not do well, sin crouches at the door; its desire is for you, but you must rule over it.”
“The valley of Achor for a door of hope.”
“Guard the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your bosom.”
At our doors are all choice fruits.
He who makes his door high seeks destruction.

evidence.locator: Num.10.3, פֶּתַח → θύραν; Lev.1.3 and Gen.18.1 the same; θύρα renders פֶּתַח ×91

evidence.note: “I am the door: if anyone enters through me he will be saved.”
“I stand at the door and knock; if anyone opens the door, I will come in to him”, in the words of Sng 5:2.
“I have set before you an open door, which no one can shut”, after the key of David (v. 7).
God had opened to the nations a door of faith.

evidence.locator: Psa.24.7, פֶּתַח → πύλαι; πύλη renders פֶּתַח ×5

evidence.note: “Enter through the narrow gate.”

parallels.note: Gate: “lift up your heads, O gates… everlasting doors”; wisdom at the gates and at the openings.
The door that closes the opening; with מְזוּזָה, the doorposts.

phrases.gloss: the entrance of the tent of meeting

senses.definition: What is cut into stone, gold or wood: the names on the high priest’s stones, “Holy to Yahweh” on his gold plate, the carved cherubim and palms of the temple’s walls, and the engraving Yahweh cuts on the stone before Joshua.

evidence.note: “The engravings of a signet”, the names of the sons of Israel on two stones.
Twelve stones, each “with the engravings of a signet, every one with his name, for the twelve tribes”.
The plate of the holy crown: “an inscription, the engravings of a signet: Holy to Yahweh.”
All the walls carved with carved engravings of cherubim and palm trees and open flowers.
The enemy broke down its carved work with axes and hammers.
“I will engrave its engraving.”

words.summary: The noun of the piel’s “engrave”. How cutting into a surface goes with opening is not shown by scripture’s use; Phoenician has the same noun, ptḥ “engraving, inscription”, beside its ptḥ “open” and ptḥ “doorway”, so the three stand in one spelling outside Hebrew too.

senses.definition: The instrument that opens a locked door; laid on the shoulder, the authority over a house, to open and shut it.

evidence.note: Eglon’s servants “took the key and opened” the locked doors of the upper room.
“I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder; he will open and none shall shut.” Rev 3:7 gives it to Christ.
The gatekeeping Levites were over the key (the opening) of the house of God, morning by morning.
“He who has the key of David”, Isa 22:22 from the Hebrew.
“I have the keys of the grave and of death.”
“I will give you the keys of the kingdom of the heavens.”
The lawyers took away the key of knowledge.

senses.gloss: opening (of the lips): what is spoken
senses.definition: The opening of the lips, the speaking itself; Wisdom’s is upright things.

evidence.note: “I will speak noble things, and the opening of my lips shall be right things”, in parallel with speaking.

words.summary: Used once, of speech. BDB’s key for it also takes the two tokens of הַמַּפְתֵּחַ “the key” (Jdg 3:25; 1Ch 9:27), so its count is three.

senses.gloss: opening of the mouth: freedom to speak
senses.definition: In פִּתְחוֹן פֶּה, the opening of the mouth: the right or boldness to speak, taken away from Jerusalem in her shame and given to Ezekiel when Israel’s horn sprouts.

evidence.note: “That you may remember and be ashamed, and never open your mouth again because of your shame, when I make a covering for you.”
“I will make a horn sprout for the house of Israel, and I will give you the opening of the mouth among them.”

senses.definition: The opening of Yahweh’s words, their being laid open, which gives light and understanding.

evidence.note: “The opening of your words gives light; it gives understanding to the simple.”

words.summary: Used once, a form beside פֶּתַח. Whether it is “the doorway” of the words, the way in to them, or their “unfolding” as the verb opens a riddle (Psa 49:5), the verse does not settle: both are opening.

senses.definition: A sword opened, drawn from the sheath: the hidden war in a smooth speaker’s words.

evidence.note: “His words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords.”

words.summary: Used once, of drawn swords; the qal uses the verb the same way (Psa 37:14; Ezk 21:33).

senses.definition: A garment of the proud daughters of Zion, to be replaced by a girding of sackcloth; set against sackcloth, it is something rich.

evidence.note: “Instead of a פְּתִיגִיל, a girding of sackcloth.”

words.summary: Used once, in a list of finery. Its ending is not a Hebrew pattern, and how it comes from this root (if from it at all) is not clear; the meaning rests only on its being set against sackcloth.

senses.definition: Of windows, to stand open; of books in the court of the Ancient of Days, to be opened for judgment.

evidence.note: Daniel’s windows were open toward Jerusalem, and he prayed three times a day.
“The court sat, and the books were opened.” Taken up in Rev 20:12.
The dead stand before God and books are opened; they are judged by what was written in them.
From Aramaic אֶתְפְּתַח, “be opened”.
Jesus said to the deaf man, “Ephphatha”, that is, “Be opened”; and his ears were opened (v. 35).

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܦܬܚ (pṯaḥ), its verb for opening where the Greek has ἀνοίγω and διανοίγω: doors, mouths, the heavens, graves, eyes and ears, books and seals.

senses.definition: To open a door, the mouth, a book or seal, a treasure; of the Lord, to open a heart or the mind to understand.

evidence.note: “I will open my mouth in parables”, Psa 78:2.
He opened his mouth and taught them.
Philip opened his mouth and, beginning from Isa 53, preached Jesus.
He who opens and no one shuts.
The magi opened their treasures.
He opened their mind to understand the scriptures.
The Lord opened Lydia’s heart to attend to what Paul said.
The Lion of the tribe of Judah has prevailed to open the book.
The earth opened its mouth, as Num 16:32.

senses.definition: Of the heavens, a door, a mouth: to be opened.

evidence.note: “Knock, and it will be opened to you.”
The heavens were opened to him.
Zechariah’s mouth was opened at once, and he spoke, blessing God.
A great door has been opened to me.
The temple of God in heaven was opened.

senses.gloss: open the eyes of the blind
senses.definition: To open blind eyes, the sign promised in Isa 35:5.

evidence.note: It was a sabbath when Jesus made clay and opened his eyes.
“Since the world began it has not been heard that anyone opened the eyes of one born blind.”
Paul sent “to open their eyes, to turn them from darkness to light”.

senses.definition: Of eyes and ears, to be opened by healing; of graves, to be opened for the dead to rise.

evidence.note: ܐܬܦܬܚ, “be opened”, the word the Greek keeps as ἐφφαθά.
His ears were opened.
Their eyes were opened.
Their eyes were opened and they knew him.
The graves were opened, and many bodies of the saints who slept arose.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܡܦܬܚܐ, the same phrase as Ezekiel’s פִּתְחוֹן פֶּה: the opening of the mouth, boldness to speak.

senses.definition: The opening of the mouth to speak the word boldly.

evidence.note: “That speech may be given me in the opening of my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܦܬܝܚܐ, “open”, as the Hebrew passive participle פָּתוּחַ.

senses.definition: Standing open: a door, a book, a grave.

evidence.note: “I have set before you an open door, which no one can shut.”
A door standing open in heaven.
A little book open in his hand.
“Their throat is an open grave”, Psa 5:10.

cognates.gloss: open, unlock (a door); begin; conquer; (VII) be opened; (V) of blossoms, open
cognates.note: Lane’s sources gloss it as the contrary of أَغْلَقَ “lock” and say it of a door; of blossoms opening (form V) as Sng 7:13; فَتْحٌ is also the conquest of a country, as a city “opens” (Deu 20:11).

evidence.note: “He opened, i. q. فَرَجَ, and [app. he unlocked,] contr. of أَغْلَقَ, a door.”
تفتّح النَّوْرُ “The blossom opened”; فَتْحٌ “Conquest of a country”.
“An opening, or intervening space; syn. فُرْجَةٌ.”
بَابٌ فُتُحٌ “A wide, open, door.”

cognates.note: The same instrument noun as מַפְתֵּחַ, from the same verb.

evidence.note: “A key; an instrument with which a lock is opened; [a key] of a door; and of anything that is closed, or locked.”

cognates.gloss: open; reveal, disclose; let flow; (of a person) unlock
cognates.note: Akkadian has lost the ḥ (leaving the vowel e), so it cannot show which older sound stands behind ח.

evidence.note: Meanings include “open”, “be opened”, “disclose”, “reveal”, “let flow”, “unlocking”, “undoing”.
“doorway; opening.”

cognates.note: An instrument noun of petû, as מַפְתֵּחַ of פָּתַח.

evidence.note: “key; small saw.”

cognates.note: Boring and piercing is near to engraving, but Akkadian keeps ḫ, so if this is the engraving sense’s cognate, that sense stands on an older ptḫ beside ptḥ “open”. Only a possibility: the Phoenician “engraving” cannot tell ḥ from ḫ.

evidence.locator: armep x000119690, patāhu [puncture] V; armep x000144850, patāhu [pierce] V
evidence.note: “pierce”; “run through (with a sword)”.

cognates.note: pth bt w ubʾa, “open the house, that I may enter” (KTU 1.100:72), with “house” as the object, as פָּתַח with doors.

evidence.note: “pth imper. ‘to open’ (H. pataḥ, yiptaḥ, Arab. fataḥa, yaftaḥu).”

evidence.locator: SEM000314 ptḥ [open] V, UGC003400; SEM000313 ptḥ [entrance] N, UGC003401

cognates.note: Tabnit’s coffin: “do not, do not open it” (KAI 13). Neo-Punic uses it for putting produce up for sale, as Amos 8:5 “open wheat”.

cognates.note: Old South Arabian: to take a town, and of a house, to be laid waste; its own note compares Arabic fataḥa “open; conquer”. It answers to the qal of a city opened to an enemy (Deu 20:11; Nam 3:13).

doctrine.statement: Yahweh says to his dead people, “I am opening your graves, and I will bring you up from your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel… and I will put my spirit in you, and you shall live” (Ezk 37:12–14). The dead are in their graves until he opens them; life is given when they are brought up and his spirit is put in them, and it is lived in the land. When Christ died, the graves were opened and bodies of the saints who slept arose (Mat 27:52), a foretaste of the hour when all in the graves will hear his voice and come out (Jhn 5:28–29).

Yahweh took the stewardship of the king’s house from Shebna and laid “the key of the house of David” on Eliakim’s shoulder: “he will open and none will shut, and he will shut and none will open” (Isa 22:20–22). Jesus applies the same words to himself: “He who has the key of David, who opens and no one shuts” (Rev 3:7), and sets before the faithful an open door that no one can shut (Rev 3:8). The authority over David’s house, given once to a steward, is held by the son of David, and he alone admits to it.

The servant of Isa 53 “was oppressed and afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth”, like a lamb led to slaughter (Isa 53:7). Philip, asked of whom the prophet spoke, began at this scripture and preached Jesus (Act 8:32–35); before the high priest and Pilate Jesus held his peace and answered not a word (Mat 26:63; 27:14), and when reviled he did not revile in return (1Pe 2:23). The servant whose ear Yahweh opened, and who did not rebel (Isa 50:5), is the same who kept his mouth shut under suffering.

Isaiah promises that when God comes to save, “the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be opened” (Isa 35:4–5). Jesus said “Ephphatha”, Be opened, and the deaf man’s ears were opened (Mrk 7:34–35); he opened the eyes of one born blind, a thing never heard of before (Jhn 9:32), and sent John’s disciples word that the blind see and the deaf hear (Mat 11:5). His works are the signs Isaiah tied to the coming of God and his kingdom.

Yahweh tells Cain, “If you do not do well, sin crouches at the door; its desire is for you, but you must rule over it” (Gen 4:7). The danger at Cain’s door is called sin, not a being apart from him; it desires him, and he is told he can and must master it. James describes the same course: each one is tempted when drawn away by his own desire, and desire conceived brings forth sin, and sin, finished, brings forth death (Jas 1:14–15); Paul likewise: “Do not let sin reign in your mortal body” (Rom 6:12).

On the seventeenth day of the second month of Noah’s six hundredth year “all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the heavens were opened” (Gen 7:11), the waters from below and above at once; they prevailed until all the high mountains under the whole heaven were covered (Gen 7:19–20). Peter takes it as history: the world that then was, overflowed with water, perished (2Pe 3:6). The flood was global, dated to the day in Noah’s life, and the same God who opened the windows of the heavens in judgment promises to open them for blessing (Mal 3:10).

Daniel saw the Ancient of Days take his seat: “the court sat, and the books were opened” (Dan 7:10). John sees the dead, small and great, stand before God, and the books opened, and the dead judged by what was written in them according to their works (Rev 20:12). Judgment is by a record already kept, laid open at the appointed time.

Every offering was to be brought to “the entrance of the tent of meeting”, and an ox slain anywhere else was blood guilt (Lev 17:3–4); there Yahweh would meet Israel and speak with them (Exo 29:42–43), and there the congregation gathered at the sound of the trumpets (Num 10:3). There was one way of approach, and Yahweh set it. Jesus says, “I am the door: if anyone enters by me, he will be saved” (Jhn 10:9), and “no one comes to the Father except through me” (Jhn 14:6).

note: Root key פתח as the corpus has it. BDB files the verb twice, q.ea.aa “open” and q.eb.aa “engrave”, with the same 147 tokens under each; the entry takes q.ea.aa only and gives the engraving sense under the piel and pual. BDB also files seven qal tokens under the noun key q.ea.ab by spelling, and the two הַמַּפְתֵּחַ tokens (Jdg 3:25; 1Ch 9:27) under both מִפְתָּח (q.ea.ai) and מַפְתֵּחַ (q.ea.aj), so both counts include them. The hithpael of Isa 52:2 (הִתְפַּתְּחִי) has no BDB key in the database. Names left out for their own entries: יִפְתָּח Jephthah (q.ea.ag; also the town Iphtah, Jos 15:43), פְּתַחְיָה Pethahiah (q.ea.af), and the places יִפְתַּח־אֵל Iphtah-el (q.ea.ah, whose key in the database wrongly takes every token of אֵל) and נֶפְתּוֹחַ Nephtoah (q.ea.ak). Not yet consulted: Leslau or Dillmann for Ge’ez (cited here from Anderson and Moser only), CAD for petû and patāḫu, Payne Smith for Syriac ܦܬܚܐ “door”. Whether the engraving sense is an older ptḫ (Akkadian patāḫu “pierce”) or ptḥ “open” in the sense of cutting open is open; the Phoenician ptḥ “engraving” beside ptḥ “open” and “doorway” keeps them together for now. Segert’s OCR writes pth; the scan should be checked for the ḥ.
